root_cause.text: dm_cache_metadata_abort() in the dm-cache metadata subsystem allocates a temporary block_manager before taking root_lock, but on the cmd_write_lock()/fail_io read-only early-exit path it jumps out without destroying that newly created block_manager, leaking the allocation on abort retries.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces the manual WRITE_LOCK/fail_io check with WRITE_LOCK_OR_GOTO(cmd, out) and the commit message explicitly states that “the temporary block_manager created outside the root_lock is not properly released,” while kmemleak traces the leaked object to dm_block_manager_create() called from dm_cache_metadata_abort().

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: dm_cache_metadata_abort() in the dm-cache metadata subsystem allocates a temporary block_manager before taking root_lock, but on the cmd_write_lock()/fail_io read-only early-exit path it jumps out without destroying that newly created block_manager, leaking the allocation on abort retries.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch replaces the manual WRITE_LOCK/fail_io check with WRITE_LOCK_OR_GOTO(cmd, out) and the commit message explicitly states that “the temporary block_manager created outside the root_lock is not properly released,” while kmemleak traces the leaked object to dm_block_manager_create() called from dm_cache_metadata_abort().

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a write-lock helper macro that jumps to a caller-provided label on lock acquisition failure to simplify shared error-handling paths.
intent_record.what: A new macro named WRITE_LOCK_OR_GOTO(cmd, label) was added, which calls cmd_write_lock(cmd) and performs a goto to the specified label if the lock acquisition fails.
intent_record.how: This provides a reusable control-flow helper for write-lock acquisition failure paths, allowing callers to branch to cleanup or error-handling labels instead of immediately returning when cmd_write_lock() fails.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the shared write-lock helper to centralize fail_io checking and early exit logic in dm_cache_metadata_abort.
intent_record.what: The code replaces an explicit WRITE_LOCK(cmd) followed by a manual check of cmd->fail_io, WRITE_UNLOCK(cmd), and goto out with a single WRITE_LOCK_OR_GOTO(cmd, out) macro call, and adds a comment stating that cmd_write_lock() already checks fail_io while holding cmd->root_lock.
intent_record.how: At runtime, lock acquisition and fail_io validation are consolidated into one helper path, so the function exits through out if write locking cannot proceed due to fail_io without duplicating the check logic locally; this preserves the early-abort behavior while ensuring the check is performed under the proper lock context.

grouping_result.intent: Use the shared write-lock helper to centralize fail_io checking and early exit logic in dm_cache_metadata_abort.

consistency_review.core_intent: Introduce and apply a shared write-lock helper that centralizes lock/fail_io error handling in dm_cache metadata abort paths.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly modify dm_cache_metadata_abort()'s write-lock/early-exit path—the same path implicated in the leak—and centralize the fail_io/lock failure handling that causes the abort routine to jump out before cleanup. This is directly tied to the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: This allocates the temporary block_manager before the lock/fail_io check. If the later early-exit path is taken, this newly allocated object is leaked because cleanup does not destroy it.
This conditional triggers the read-only early-exit path after allocation, causing the function to bypass destruction of the newly created block_manager.
This jump exits through a path that does not clean up the newly allocated temporary block_manager, directly embodying the leak on abort retries.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement allocates the temporary block_manager before the fail_io/read-only check. On the later early-exit path, the function jumps out without destroying new_bm, causing the leak described in the root cause.
This jump takes the early-exit path after fail_io is detected, but exits without destroying the newly allocated new_bm, making the allocation leak persistent across abort retries.
This condition guards the read-only early-exit path that is reachable after new_bm has already been allocated, enabling the control flow that bypasses cleanup of the temporary block_manager.

commit 352b837a5541690d4f843819028cf2b8be83d424
Author: Mike Snitzer <snitzer@kernel.org>
Date:   Wed Nov 30 13:26:32 2022 -0500

    dm cache: Fix ABBA deadlock between shrink_slab and dm_cache_metadata_abort
    
    Same ABBA deadlock pattern fixed in commit 4b60f452ec51 ("dm thin: Fix
    ABBA deadlock between shrink_slab and dm_pool_abort_metadata") to
    DM-cache's metadata.
    
    Reported-by: Zhihao Cheng <chengzhihao1@huawei.com>
    Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
    Fixes: 028ae9f76f29
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because it fully contains the relevant allocation, early-exit, and cleanup logic for dm_cache_metadata_abort(). In this commit, the function allocates `new_bm = dm_block_manager_create(...)` before taking `WRITE_LOCK(cmd)`, then explicitly handles the read-only early-exit path: `if (cmd->fail_io) { WRITE_UNLOCK(cmd); goto out; }`. At label `out:`, it cleans up the temporary allocation with `if (new_bm && !IS_ERR(new_bm)) dm_block_manager_destroy(new_bm);`. This directly addresses the stated root cause of leaking a newly created block_manager on the `cmd_write_lock()/fail_io` early-exit path. The function also destroys the old block manager after unlock via `dm_block_manager_destroy(old_bm);`, and uses `__destroy_persistent_data_objects(cmd, false)` so it does not destroy `cmd->bm` while still needing explicit lifecycle control. Therefore, the vulnerable construct is not present in this version, and the fix is present.
